facts.text: Côte Saint-Luc's master plan process covers the potential redevelopment of Quartier Cavendish, the CSL Shopping Centre and Décarie Square.
facts.evidence: Côte St. Luc held meetings in July, August and September 2024 in connection with its master plan for the future of the city, including the potential redevelopment of Quartier Cavendish, the CSL Shopping Centre and Décarie Square.

facts.text: The City of Côte Saint-Luc and Mandevco, the developer of Quartier Cavendish, are not yet aligned on a potential redevelopment of the mall site.
facts.evidence: The City of Côte St. Luc and Mandevco, the developer of Quartier Cavendish, are not yet agreed on the city's position regarding a potential redevelopment of the mall site.

facts.text: Côte Saint-Luc is a mostly residential suburb forming an enclave within Montreal, and a Canadian Pacific Railway marshalling yard lies within its borders.
facts.evidence: Côte Saint-Luc is a city on the Island of Montreal... a mostly residential suburb of Montreal within which it forms an enclave. The Canadian Pacific Railway Marshalling yard is situated within its borders.

overview: Côte Saint-Luc had 34,504 residents in the 2021 Census, up 6.3 percent from 32,448 in 2016, packed into just 7.04 square kilometres. That makes it a very dense market, where most customers live within a short drive or walk of any local business.

The city is mostly residential and largely English-speaking, with an older population. Its shopping centres are being reconsidered for redevelopment, so local retail and services face a period of change as new housing and a town centre are planned.
